title: SOC memory — a run's working memory
description:
What the run currently believes, what it has ruled out, and what it means to do next. Distinct from campaign state and from cross-run memory, and the distinction is the whole design: `frame-state-v1` holds STATUSES, which only an admission may move; cross-run memory holds what survives a campaign; this holds ATTENTION, which is allowed to be wrong. Attention that can never be wrong is not attention, it is evidence — so this file may hold a hunch, and may never hold a status.

The structure is canonical and the rendered `.soc` text is a projection of it. That order matters: the predecessor stored free text and parsed it back with regexes, which made a speculative insight and a kernel-grounded one indistinguishable to a reader and to a parser.

target_sha256.description: The frozen target this memory is about. A soc file that is not bound to a target drifts onto the next problem and carries its conclusions there — which is how a run inherits confidence it never earned.

current.description: The single thing being pursued right now. One line each, because a CURRENT section listing five active moves is a section describing no decision.

insights.description: What the run believes, each carrying the strongest status any EVIDENCE supports — not the strength of the belief. The tier orders attention and never confers trust: writing VERIFIED here does not make anything verified, and only an admission through the reducer can.

tier.description: A frame status, not a parallel vocabulary. The predecessor invented VERIFIED/CHECKED/CONJECTURAL alongside the status lattice, which meant two ladders with different rungs and no rule connecting them.

evidence_ref.description: What backs it, if anything does. An insight above CONJECTURE with no evidence_ref is refused: the tier is a claim about evidence, so a tier with no evidence behind it is the exact laundering this file exists to prevent.

failed_approaches.description: What has been ruled out, and why. This is the section that pays for the file: without it the twentieth attempt knows what the first one knew.

revival_condition.description: What would make this worth trying again. A route closed with no revival condition is closed forever, which is rarely what anyone meant.

decisions.description: Choices made, with the options that were available and the reason. Recorded BEFORE the outcome is known — a decision log written afterwards records the justification rather than the reasoning.

reward.description: What the choice turned out to be worth, attributed after the fact. This is the only thing that makes the memory LEARN rather than merely accumulate.

queue.description: What is planned. A queue that is never emptied is a wish list; entries carry a state so a stalled one is visible.

consolidations.description: What consolidation removed and why. A memory that compacts silently is a memory whose reader cannot tell forgetting from never-knowing.
